question: Should five consecutive syntactically malformed Google Meet pullAudio payloads consume the existing transient input-error budget and close the active bridge?
rationale: The code and proof establish correct validation, but repository policy treats new fail-closed runtime behavior and availability loss as an owner decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Keep the five-error cutoff
options.body: Treat repeated malformed responses as a broken paired-node bridge, retain valid-chunk counter reset, and close after five consecutive failures.

options.title: Drop malformed chunks without shutdown
options.body: Reject and log malformed chunks but keep them outside the transport-error budget so an active bridge remains open indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Keep the five-error cutoff
recommendation.body: Treat repeated malformed responses as a broken paired-node bridge, retain valid-chunk counter reset, and close after five consecutive failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Google Meet realtime and Chrome-node audio ownership most directly covers this failure-policy choice.
